title: Instrument Air Dryer
model_title: Instrument Air Dryer — Twin-Tower Heated Blower-Purge Desiccant Type

introduction.definition: An instrument air dryer removes water vapour from compressed air so control valves, positioners and instruments never see condensation, corrosion or ice. This twin-tower heated blower-purge type dries air in one desiccant tower while the other is regenerated by ambient air from a blower, heated to ≈ 150–200 °C and passed counter-flow through the wet bed; little or no dried compressed air is spent on purging.
applications: Instrument air for refineries, chemical, power and alumina plants
Dry air for pneumatic conveying, blanketing and outdoor lines in cold climates
key_points: Adsorption at pressure, regeneration by heat
Counter-current regeneration keeps outlet end driest
introduction.summary: An instrument air dryer removes water vapour from compressed air so control valves and instruments never see condensation or ice. working_principle.characteristic_curve: Outlet dew point vs time through a cycle.

temperature.title: Heat drives the water off the desiccant
temperature.description: In the regenerating tower, ambient air from the blower is heated (≈ 150–200 °C) and passed down through the bed, opposite to the drying flow, so the wettest desiccant at the inlet end is heated last and the outlet end stays driest. The heat front moves through the bed, then the tower is cooled and repressurised before switching. Compared with heatless dryers (≈ 15 % purge of dried air), blower-purge dryers use little or no compressed air. Instrument air is typically dried to a pressure dew point of about −40 °C (ISO 8573-1 class 2).

script.narration: This module introduces the Instrument Air Dryer.
An instrument air dryer removes water vapour from compressed air so control valves, positioners and instruments never see condensation, corrosion or ice.

This twin-tower heated blower-purge type dries air in one desiccant tower while the other is regenerated by ambient air from a blower, heated to ≈ 150–200 °C and passed counter-flow through the wet bed; little or no dried compressed air is spent on purging.
Typical applications include instrument air for refineries, chemical, power and alumina plants; dry air for pneumatic conveying, blanketing and outdoor lines in cold climates.

video_tutorials.title: Instrument Air Dryer — Operation

script.narration: How the Instrument Air Dryer works.
Wet air passes the coalescing pre-filter.
It flows up through the drying tower; desiccant adsorbs water.
The moisture front rises through the bed.
Blower and heater regenerate the other tower counter-flow.
Dry air leaves through the after-filter; valves switch towers.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

In the regenerating tower, ambient air from the blower is heated (≈ 150–200 °C) and passed down through the bed, opposite to the drying flow, so the wettest desiccant at the inlet end is heated last and the outlet end stays driest.

video_tutorials.title: Instrument Air Dryer — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Instrument Air Dryer.
Check dew point, ΔP and drains.
Change filter elements; test switching valves.
Replace desiccant (≈ 3 – 5 years); service blower and heater.
Watch for wet air downstream: dew point rises, water in lines. Common cause: oil-fouled desiccant.
Watch for desiccant dusting: after-filter ΔP rises. Common cause: bed fluidisation by fast depressurisation.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
